labels.text: Usage: /search <question>, answer from a web search
/search needs a web search key in this session

S57.01.needs: a web search key saved in the CLI (Brave or Tavily), or a model that can search the web
S57.01.note: The code shows the query on the tool line; I did not confirm where the sources are listed.
steps: Start agi in a terminal.
Type /search and a question that needs current web facts, then press Enter.
Look for a tool line for web_search that shows the query.
Compare the answer and any listed sources with Expected.
S57.01.where: agi, then type /search followed by a question that needs current web facts

S57.02.note: There is no command for this tool; the assistant calls it when a request needs a page.
steps: Start agi.
Type a request that gives a web page address and asks what the page says, then press Enter.
Look for a tool line named web_fetch that shows the address.
Check that the answer uses text from that page.
S57.02.where: agi, then ask in chat for the content of a web page by its address

S57.03.needs: a PDF or Office file in the folder
S57.03.note: The code reads these files through read_file; I did not confirm the exact preview text for each format.
steps: Start agi in a folder that holds a PDF, Word, PowerPoint or Excel file.
Type a request that names the file and asks for part of its text, then press Enter.
Look for a read_file tool line that shows the file path.
Check that the answer quotes text from that file.
S57.03.where: agi, then ask in chat to read a PDF or Office file by its path

S57.04.needs: a folder with a few text files, one containing a known word
S57.04.note: There is no separate search control; the assistant calls the tool.
steps: Start agi in a folder with a few text files.
Type a request to find files that contain a word you know is in one of them, then press Enter.
Look for a search_files or grep_files tool line that shows the pattern.
Check that the answer lists the matching paths.
S57.04.where: agi, then ask in chat to find files by name or by text

S57.05.needs: a text file in the folder
steps: Start agi in a folder with a text file.
Type a request to read that file by name, then press Enter.
Look for a read_file tool line that shows the path.
Check that the answer matches the file's contents.
S57.05.where: agi, then ask in chat to read a named file

S57.06.needs: a folder agi may write to
steps: Start agi in a folder that agi may write to.
Type a request to create a file named notes.txt with one line of text, then press Enter.
If the Tool Approval box appears, choose Yes.
Look for a write_file tool line that shows the path, then check that notes.txt exists in the folder.
S57.06.where: agi, then ask in chat to create a file

S57.10.note: No separate code-execution tool was found; the script runs through the shell tool (run_command).
steps: Start agi.
Type a request to write a short Python script that prints 2 plus 2 and to run it, then press Enter.
If the Tool Approval box appears, choose Yes.
Look for a line starting with $ and the printed result, and an exit line.
S57.10.where: agi, then ask in chat to write and run a short Python script

S57.11.needs: a Mac or Linux shell with ls
steps: Start agi in a folder with some files.
Type a request to run the command ls -la in this folder, then press Enter.
If the Tool Approval box appears, choose Yes.
Look for a line starting with $ ls -la, the listing, and an exit 0 line.
S57.11.where: agi, then ask in chat to run a shell command

S57.12.needs: a text file with three lines
S57.12.note: The tool name edit_file appears in the catalog; I did not confirm how the diff is drawn beyond the edit result code.
steps: Create a text file with three lines in the folder.
Type a request to change the second line of that file to say hello, then press Enter.
If the Tool Approval box appears, choose Yes.
Look for the edit tool line and the changed line, and check the other lines are unchanged.
S57.12.where: agi, then ask in chat to change one line of an existing file

S57.13.needs: AGI Desktop with its Chrome extension paired
S57.13.note: Pairing state is shown by /chrome; I did not check the pairing steps themselves.
steps: Start agi.
Type /chrome and press Enter.
Look for the Chrome integration text and a Paired line.
Type a request to open https://example.com in the browser, then press Enter.
Look for an Open line in the transcript that shows the address.
S57.13.where: agi, then type /chrome, then ask in chat to open a web page in the browser

S57.14.needs: AGI Desktop with its Chrome extension paired and a page open
S57.14.note: Clicking and typing use the same route with other browser tool names; the read line is the one given here.
steps: Start agi with the browser paired (see /chrome).
Type a request to read the text of the page open in the browser, then press Enter.
Look for a transcript line that says Read the active tab.
Compare the answer with the text on the page.
S57.14.where: agi, then type /chrome, then ask in chat to read the page open in the browser

S57.16.needs: an account that can generate images
S57.16.note: I did not confirm whether the image also appears inline in the transcript.
steps: Start agi.
Type /image a red bicycle on a beach, then press Enter.
Wait for the generation to finish; a chip appears.
Type /image open to view the image.
Compare the image with the prompt.
S57.16.where: agi, then type /image followed by a short description

S57.21.note: The assistant's memory tool is called by the model during a turn; this path covers the user's view of the same memory.
steps: Start agi.
Type /memory and press Enter to see saved facts.
Type /memory add local and a short test fact, then press Enter.
Type /memory again and check that the new fact is listed.

S57.22.needs: a managed account with Google Calendar connected on the connectors page
S57.22.note: No dedicated calendar tool was found in the CLI; calendar access comes through a connector.
steps: Start agi on a managed account.
Type /connectors and press Enter.
Check that the text says connectors are offered to this session's turns.
Ask in chat about today's calendar events, then check for a tool line and an approval box before it runs.

S57.23.needs: a managed account with Slack connected on the connectors page
S57.23.note: No dedicated messaging tool was found in the CLI; Slack access comes through a connector.
steps: Start agi on a managed account.
Type /connectors and press Enter.
Check that the text lists the connectors offered to this session.
Ask in chat to read the latest Slack message, then check for a tool line and an approval box before it runs.

S57.24.needs: a managed account that can use cloud schedules
S57.24.note: The delete and list actions use cron_delete and cron_list; I did not walk through them.
steps: Start agi on an account that can use cloud schedules.
Type /schedule every day at 9am summarize today's notes, then press Enter.
Approve the schedule creation if asked.
Look for a cron_create tool line and confirm the new schedule is listed when you ask for your schedules.
S57.24.where: agi, then type /schedule followed by what to run and when

S57.25.needs: at least one agent file, made with /agents create
steps: Start agi.
Type /agents and press Enter; an agent picker opens.
Pick an agent, or press Esc to close the picker.
Ask in chat to use a named agent, then look for an agent tool line that shows its name.

S57.26.note: The plan marked this unverified; the ask_user tool and its question box were found in the code.
steps: Start agi in an interactive terminal.
Type a request asking the assistant to ask you which of two options you want, then press Enter.
Look for a question box that shows the choices.
Pick one and check that the assistant continues with that choice.
S57.26.where: agi, then ask in chat for a question with choices

steps: Start agi.
Type a request asking the assistant to get my approval of a plan before doing anything, then press Enter.
Look for the Tool Approval box with a question.
Choose Yes and check that the assistant continues; choose No and check that it stops.
S57.27.where: agi, then ask in chat for approval of a plan

S57.28.note: The note to the model about on-demand tools is in the system prompt and is not shown to the user.
steps: Start agi.
Type /tools and press Enter.
Check the line that says Tools the model can call in this session with a count.
Ask a request that needs a tool not on that list and look for a tool_search line in the transcript.
S57.28.where: not visible in the app; the list of tools the model can call appears under /tools

S57.29.note: Keyword search is run by the model; the user has no search box. /tools lists all tools and /tools <name> needs an exact name.
steps: Start agi.
Type a request that asks the assistant to find tools about files, then press Enter.
Look for a tool_search tool line in the transcript.
Check that the result lists matching tool names with descriptions.
S57.29.where: agi, then ask in chat for a tool by topic

steps: Start agi.
Type /tools and press Enter to see the list of tools with descriptions.
Type /tools read_file and press Enter.
Check that the name, description, and a Parameters: section with the schema appear.
Start agi.
Type a request to run the command echo hello, then press Enter.
Look at the tool line; it should show the command after a $ sign.
If the Tool Approval box appears, check it shows the command before you choose Yes or No.
S57.31.where: agi, then ask in chat to run a command or change a file

S57.32.note: The code shows the counts text; I did not confirm exactly where on screen it is drawn.
steps: Start agi.
Type a request to run the command sleep 5, then press Enter.
While it runs, look for a spinner on the tool line and the elapsed time in brackets.
When it finishes, look for a check mark for completed or a cross for failed, and the counts with working and completed.
S57.32.where: agi, then ask in chat for any request that runs a tool

S57.33.note: The full output is shown with Ctrl-O, which is outside this item.
steps: Start agi in a folder with a few files.
Type a request to list the files in this folder, then press Enter.
Look for a short preview line under the tool line.
Check that the preview shows the first non-empty line of the result, shortened if long.
S57.33.where: agi, then ask in chat for any request that runs a tool

labels.text: Show or hide full tool output
showing full tool output, Ctrl-O to collapse

S57.34.needs: a Free account or paid account with a model that can call a shell tool
S57.34.note: Ctrl-O toggles every tool output in the transcript at once, not one call. The expanded view shows the result only, not the arguments; arguments are shown through "/tools log <n>" (S57.37), so Expected's "full arguments" is not met by Ctrl-O alone.
steps: Run agi and start a chat that makes a tool call (for example a shell command with several lines of output).
Find the finished tool call in the transcript and note its short result preview.
Press Ctrl-O. The status line shows "showing full tool output, Ctrl-O to collapse" and the output lines appear, up to 200, then "… N more lines" if longer.
Press Ctrl-O again. The status line shows "tool output collapsed" and the preview returns. Compare with Expected: the call expands and collapses.
S57.34.where: agi (chat screen), then press Ctrl-O; the key list in "/help" shows "Show or hide full tool output"

labels.text: /tools retry reruns the last failed call
No failed tool call in this session to retry.

S57.35.needs: a Free account or paid account with a model; a way to make a tool call fail
S57.35.note: The code shows the user-side retry (/tools retry). The failed-state mark is in apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs ("✗" for TranscriptCellState::Failed). I did not confirm from the code that the error text is sent back to the model on its own, only that the retry prompt is built from the failed call; Expected's 'error goes back to the model' is therefore unverified.
steps: Run agi and ask the assistant for a tool call that fails (for example reading a file that does not exist).
Look for the failed call in the transcript; its state shows as a red failed mark with the error.
Type /tools retry and press Enter. The assistant is sent a prompt to run the failed call again and report the result.
If no call failed, look for the message "No failed tool call in this session to retry." Compare with Expected: the error is shown, and the retry runs.
S57.35.where: agi (chat screen), then type /tools retry; the list shown by "/tools" says "/tools retry reruns the last failed call"

labels.text: [full output saved for the user to

S57.36.needs: a Free account or paid account with a model that can run a shell command; a command with large output
S57.36.note: The code stores the output in the config folder's tool-output directory and tells the model that read_file cannot open it. The Expected line says the model can open it later, which the code contradicts; the tester should check that point against the notice text. The exact path is built at run time, so no fixed path is given.
steps: Run agi and ask the assistant to run a shell command that prints a very large amount of text (thousands of lines).
Look at the end of that tool result in the transcript for the notice that begins "[full output saved for the user to".
Open the path shown in the notice (in Finder or Terminal) and check that the full output is there.

Try asking the assistant to read that path with its file-read tool. Compare with Expected: the full text is stored and a reference is given; the code says the file-read tool cannot open it, so the reference is for the user only.
S57.36.where: agi (chat screen): a long tool result shows a notice at its end that begins "[full output saved for the user to" and gives a file path under the config folder's tool-output directory

labels.text: /tools log <n> shows one call in full.

S57.37.needs: a Free account or paid account with a model; the calls must be made in the same session
S57.37.note: The log reads the tool calls of the current session (session_tool_runs). The code does not show it kept after the session ends, so a tester should check whether a resumed session still lists older calls.
steps: Run agi and make two or three tool calls in the chat (for example a shell command and a file read).
Type /tools log and press Enter. A numbered list shows each call with its name, input and outcome.
Type /tools log 1 (or another number) and press Enter. It shows the call's name, its input as JSON, and its result, marked "(failed)" if it failed.
Compare with Expected: each call's tool, input and outcome can be reviewed afterwards.
S57.37.where: agi (chat screen), then type /tools log; then /tools log <n> for one call in full
